reason: The cited evidence supports the general role of Cr2O3 in corrosion resistance (E1) and notes Cr vulnerability in molten salts (E2), but it does not directly support the premise that increasing Cr content leads to rapid, uniform, stable Cr2O3 formation and reduced corrosion in aggressive environments; E3 even suggests Cr depletion is a problem and highlights alternative mechanisms (sacrificial Al, redox control), which contradicts the hypothesis's reliance on Cr alone.
premises: Cr2O3 passivation film provides excellent corrosion resistance in stainless steels and Fe-Cr alloys
Higher Cr content increases availability of Cr atoms at the surface for preferential oxidation
Cr2O3 film acts as a barrier to corrosive species, reducing dissolution and corrosion rates
Cr is the most vulnerable alloying element to fluoride salt corrosion in nuclear alloys
Cr dissolution and depletion can be mitigated by sacrificial elements or redox control
